D-BAND-ENFORCE.rationale: A wave whose own gate set classifies high-risk (carries a jury / cross-vendor / visual-band gate) keeps verify enforcement after the band-conditional merge even when it is not in a UI band; the resolver narrows enforce to advisory only for low-risk (MECH/MED) non-band waves. D-BAND-ENFORCE.title: Fleet high-risk waves keep verify enforce after band merge

D-I21-RATIFY.title: Ratify the I21 burst and retire the daemonless waiver mode

D-I25-EU-EXCLUDE.rationale: The EU rows this iter recorded measure the repair of the measure, not the work. W26 and W28 were captured under the wall-clock basis (measure v1), which counted the operator asleep at a permission prompt as agent runtime and inflated them roughly fourfold. W35 and W36 both recorded 0.3769 EU / 3.10 USD and W39 through W42 all recorded 0.0419 EU: one session's runtime handed whole to every wave that shared it (fixed in W46, which cannot retro-split a closed row). W34 closed in the same turn it was claimed, so no Stop boundary fired and it banked a zero from a process error. W39 through W42 are truncated by the measure re-origin that W42 introduced (counter_resets 1), so each closed on a floor rather than a measure. Every row is an honest record of what was captured and none of them is a reference class. From W47 on, a wave whose runtime was re-originated or shared carries calibration_excluded on the ActualSummary so a consumer skips it from state alone; the rows closed before that flag existed are the ones this decision enumerates.
D-I25-EU-EXCLUDE.title: Exclude the P30-I25 actuals from EU calibration

D-I25-ODR-DRAIN.rationale: This supersedes D-ODR-ADVISORY which rested on a false premise. That decision claimed the odr_blocking flag had been inert since it was written because the profile verify-block merge dropped it. It had not: the flag reaches the close path through the repo-config overlay and not through the profile merge, so it has been armed since P30-I23-W25 when the repo opted in after draining the I20 and I21 legacy corpus. The P30-I25-W48 merge repair recovered only PROFILE-declared fields which no shipped profile sets. Verified by running the pre-W48 loader against the pre-flip config: odr_blocking still resolved to true. What actually happened is that the repair-burst waves of P30-I25 were authored with legacy-string criteria under criteria-floor waivers so the iter reintroduced 214 untyped required criteria and its Oracle-Determinism-Ratio was 0.0 against the 0.8 floor. The honest remedy is the one the repo already uses: eawf spec convert-legacy P30-I25 typed all 214 rows with a falsifying criterion_in_diff gate and zero refusals so the iter closes with the gate ARMED AND SATISFIED rather than lowered. The config keeps odr_blocking true. A separate finding stands on its own: P30-I24 closed with an ODR of 0.000 while the gate was armed which means that close went around it; backlog B108 carries it.
D-I25-ODR-DRAIN.title: Drain the I25 criteria rather than lower the ODR gate

D-LOCK-SPLIT.rationale: Verify-then-commit split: the deterministic tier + floor pack pre-flight run OUTSIDE the state lock; the jury/LLM tier stays UNDER the lock but wall-clock-bounded. The jury tier mutates state in-memory and appends session events, so pre-flighting it needs re-apply machinery deferred to P31 verifier maturation. Splitting only the deterministic tier removes the long-hold close deadlock class (5 wedge episodes on 2026-07-01).
D-LOCK-SPLIT.title: Split wave close: deterministic pre-flight outside the state lock

D-ODR-ADVISORY.rationale: The Oracle-Determinism-Ratio scores what fraction of a scope's required criteria are falsified by a reproducible automated oracle (tiers T1 through T5) rather than by a judgment oracle (an approval or a jury reading prose). This repo scores 0.0: every required criterion is a grandfathered legacy string with no oracle tier, so every close rests on someone reading prose. The repo config set verify.odr_blocking to true, but the field was silently dropped by the profile verify-block merge and so gated nothing from the day it was written; P30-I25-W48 fixed the merge and the flag became live, at which point iter close began refusing every iter in the repo. The precondition the field's own contract states is that a profile opts in only after its legacy sub-floor criteria have been drained, and 0 of 214 required criteria in this iter are drained. Setting the flag to false records what the system has actually done since the flag shipped rather than asserting a policy the repo cannot satisfy. The gate re-arms when criteria carry deterministic oracle tiers; backlog item B-ODR-DRAIN carries that campaign. This is a policy statement about an unmet precondition and not a weakening of verification: the close-time auditor, the criteria floor, and the zero-runtime gate are all unaffected.
D-ODR-ADVISORY.title: Keep the ODR gate advisory until the legacy criteria are typed

D-RESET-PARDON-STRICT.rationale: W52 was authored with a criterion asking that the reset pardon key on whether a capture reported new counters rather than on when it arrived so that a no-op capture cannot strand a re-originated wave. Implementing it as written would weaken the gate and the criterion is therefore superseded. Two states are byte-identical in state.json: an honest reset followed by a capture that measured nothing and a capture path that is alive but reporting a frozen snapshot. Both show the same counters and a later captured_at. A rule that pardons on frozen counters closes the second case in silence which is the original defect of this entire iter where every wave recorded zero effort units for months and nobody noticed. A rule that refuses it costs an explicit no-runtime waiver which is recorded on the wave and visible in review. Silence is the failure this iter exists to eliminate and a waiver is not silence so the strict clock-based rule stands. The wave is not stranded either way because the re-origin guarantees it stays measurable going forward and a later capture that measures something closes it without any waiver at all.
D-RESET-PARDON-STRICT.title: Keep the reset pardon strict and pay for it with a visible waiver

D-RPC-TERMINAL.rationale: On close-RPC TimeoutError the CLI exits non-zero with a typed terminal error; the daemon may still be mid-close under the state lock, so falling back creates the dual-writer + ungated-close compound (harm-register A3 / ZD-R5). RuntimeError/OSError transport failures may still fall back, but the fallback close is stamped with a distinct close_mechanism value (daemon-fallback) so audits can tell the paths apart.
D-RPC-TERMINAL.title: Close-RPC timeout is terminal, never a fallback-close trigger

D-W43-CRITERIA-SUPERSEDED.rationale: P30-I25-W43 shipped two criteria that the delivered code deliberately does not satisfy and the wave is CLOSED so its criteria are immutable. CR-02 promised that the turn still in flight falls back to its row span. The implementation dropped the fallback on purpose: spanning the in-flight turn charges that turn's approval stalls back into the measure and makes the duration DROP when Claude's smaller figure lands which reads as a counter reset and re-origins the wave. It reports zero for an unmeasured turn rather than a guess and the turn is counted at the next capture. CR-03 promised that rows are ordered by timestamp before being grouped into turns. There is no sorting and no grouping because the measure no longer derives turn spans at all; it sums the turn_duration rows Claude writes and a sum is order-independent so the goal holds vacuously. Both departures are improvements on the criteria as written and both were verified by audit 4. This decision records the supersession so a reader comparing the wave contract to the code finds the reason in state rather than concluding the wave under-delivered. The duration ceiling that CR-04 promised was genuinely absent and is repaired by W49 rather than superseded here.
D-W43-CRITERIA-SUPERSEDED.title: Record that the delivered turn measure supersedes two of W43's criteria

D-WINDOWS-DESCOPE.rationale: The win32 SID-verify path has never run a real win32 round-trip (ZD-R10 / harm-register H12: validate on real win32 or explicitly de-scope). The W36 re-close runbook carries the release-notes line-item.
D-WINDOWS-DESCOPE.title: De-scope Windows in v0.6.0 notes; real win32 validation in P31

D-WINDOWS-REALHOST.rationale: D-WINDOWS-DESCOPE deferred Windows because the win32 SID-verify path had never run a real win32 round-trip. The first real run proved the suspicion: the transport shipped six defects, each a call that could not have succeeded once. ImpersonateNamedPipeClient and EqualSid were invoked through modules that do not define them, so the peer-SID check raised AttributeError on every verified connection and the worker closed the pipe; because the daemon's own ping is SID-verified, cold start could never complete. The readiness probe truth-tested a pywin32 call that returns None on success, so it reported every healthy pipe as unready. The listener returned from start before binding the first pipe instance. stop left subscription feeds on the bus. A design test asserted a win32 BOOL is the False singleton. With those fixed the win32 set passes on a real Windows host (65 passed, 4 skipped), so the de-scope premise no longer holds. This row also supersedes D-WINDOWS-VALIDATED, a placeholder a probe command created in error.
D-WINDOWS-REALHOST.title: Windows real-host validation discharged; win32 transport passes

D-WINPIPE-01.rationale: The Windows named-pipe transport reads one bounded 64KB chunk before the post-connect SID verify because ImpersonateNamedPipeClient requires a prior read to establish the client security context. The owner-only pipe DACL is the primary gate (the kernel refuses a non-owner CreateFile before any read), so the pre-verify read is reachable only by a process the kernel already attributes to the owning user; the bytes are bounded and discarded on rejection, nothing is parsed or dispatched pre-verify. Accept the residual rather than reorder (which makes the SID verify unreliable).
D-WINPIPE-01.title: Accept one bounded 64KB pre-verify pipe read; DACL is the gate

D01.rationale: Plan §4 lists P06 as Hardening + GA (Linux polish, golden scenarios, release tag). Phase 6 reframed to (a) internalize the v0.1 design spec into docs/, (b) dogfood eawf on its own repo, (c) ship the v0.1 PR. The displaced hardening work is captured in v0.2 backlog items B001 (Linux CI matrix), B009 (golden scenarios), B010 (v0.1.0 release tag).
D01.title: P06 rescope: spec internalization + dogfood instead of plan §4

D02.rationale: Bottleneck is non-coders authoring audits, not expressing arbitrary logic. YAML + registry of built-in kinds (file_exists, regex_match, json_path_value, pytest_pass, coverage_min, numeric_threshold, command_exit_zero) lets check-authors stay in YAML; new kinds are a code change. Hybrid escape hatch can come later if real example pushes against the registry.
D02.title: B019 audit-check DSL: yaml declarative + check-kind registry

D03.rationale: Audit link gates the commitment, not the exploration. Forcing audit at hypothesis open time forces premature audit design; making it fully optional fails the verify-before-claim rule. Permissive open + required audit on set-verdict matches the dogfood workflow.
D03.title: B020 hypothesis lifecycle: audit-link required at set-verdict only

D04.rationale: Local file integrity is cheap to enforce; URL integrity is a different problem (provenance + fetch policy). Mandatory-everywhere couples the registry to network state at registration. eawf artifact verify recomputes on demand for both cases.
D04.title: B021 artifact registry: sha256 mandatory for files, optional for URLs

D05.rationale: Phase close is the natural integrity boundary; manual run is the escape hatch for debugging. Every-mutation is too slow on hot paths like wave dispatch; manual-only is easy to forget. Failures block phase close; --force requires audit reason so the bypass is recorded.
D05.title: B022 integrity runner: auto on phase close + opt-in eawf validate

D06.rationale: v0.1 CLI lacks 'eawf audit set-verdict' and 'eawf backlog set-priority' verbs. Hand-editing state.json would violate AGENTS.md rule 4 (state CLI is the only mutator). Safer to ship the verbs in P07 and do the retro-stamping (A01..A06 verdicts; B015/B017 P2->P1) at P07 closeout in one pass.
D06.title: Defer retro audit-verdict + backlog priority-bumps to P07 CLI

D07.rationale: Squash collapses per-wave/per-commit history into a single fat commit on main, losing the symbol-prefixed audit trail (e.g. [P06-W05] [P06-CORE]) that AGENTS.md commit-prefix rule and the wave/audit chain depend on for reconstructibility from git log. Rebase-merge preserves linear, individual commits with their original messages — matches the cherry-pick discipline that already feeds the long-running phase branch. Merge-commits forbidden by repo settings (mergeCommitAllowed=false). Default for all phase PRs unless explicitly overridden.
D07.title: PR merge strategy: rebase-and-merge; never squash, never merge-commit

D08.rationale: User proposed shifting from per-phase PR to review-driven + version-bump PR mid-v0.2. Mid-stream workflow change = state-of-record drift risk; defer re-evaluation to v0.2.0 cut, when iter/phase aggregation pattern is fully exercised.
D08.title: Defer PR-cadence policy change until v0.2.0 ship

D09.rationale: v0.2 scope locked at P13; PyPI publish needs maintainer-track decision + CI release gating + tag-driven workflow not yet in place. Park behind tag v0.2.0 ship and reopen as v0.3 epic.

D10.rationale: D08 deferred the cadence policy revisit to v0.2.0 ship. Reviewed at P13 open: one-PR-per-phase produced clean rebase-merge history across P07..P12 and aligns with AGENTS.md phase lifecycle. Keep cadence; reopen for v0.3 only if multi-phase PRs become necessary.
D10.title: Revisit D08 — keep one-PR-per-phase cadence through v0.2 close

D30.rationale: UI/UX behaviour cannot be fully pinned by deterministic tests so a markdown-spec LLM-jury scores the residual. The gameability red-team proved naive jury gates are gameable via provenance-free evidence and deterministic-decidable rubric items; so deterministic gates rank first, the jury judges only the true residual on provenance-pinned evidence, and discrimination is proven by a deterministic canned-ballot gate not a jury. Producer and jury un-idle for the UI/UX band only via a scoped verify block not the global enforce flip.
D30.title: I08 QC gate is deterministic-first with a jury for the true residual
